To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the results of Ureaquant and EH methods are reliable and can be used in the routine analysis, and the BI method requires methodological modification for the improvement of its reliability.
the use of specific standard samples is recommended for the control of the reliability of the MUC determination by all methods (BI; EH and UR) except for FT-MIR.
the use of the specific artificial samples is a useful and reliable method for the evaluation and control of MUC analysis results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of MUC analysis results by various methods with the use of specially modified milk samples with the absence of lactose.
the reliability of results of MUC determination by various methods with the use of specially modified standard samples.

the evaluation of the reliability of the results of MUC analysis by different methods with the use of specially developed samples on a milk base with the absence of soluble components such as lactoses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ureakvant method was the most reliable and suitable for routine MUC analyses.
the Ureakvant method is the most reliable method for determination of MUC, followed by the BI and EH methods.
the results of all the tested methods are unreliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the MUC analysis by the UR method are the most reliable and the most suitable for the evaluation of milk quality and health and reproduction status of dairy cows.
the UR method was the most reliable in the determination of MUC in artificial milk samples.

it was possible to use the artificial milk control samples for the control of MUC determination in all the tested methods with the exception of the FT-MIR method, where the presence of the lactose in samples is necessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of artificial samples for the control of the MUC determination is possible and necessary, and the specific Ureakvant procedure is the most appropriate for this aim.
the results of MUC analyses are reliable and comparable with the use of standard artificial milk samples.
the results of MUC analyses by the BI method with diacetyl monoxime and FT-IR are unreliable.
